cards.text: Jehu, Israel's new king, gathers all the people for a big announcement. Then he says it: "Ahab served Baal a little, but Jehu will serve him a lot." That's like the new manager saying, "The last guy took a lot of days off? Oh, watch me take MORE."

cards.question: Jehu orders every prophet, servant and priest of Baal summoned, with nobody missing. What does he say he has planned for Baal?
And for any of Baal's prophets, servants or priests who don't show up, what does Jehu say will happen?

cards.text: Now hold on, friend. Right here the text pulls us aside and tells us what's REALLY going on with Jehu's big Baal announcement.

cards.question: Jehu is truly planning to serve Baal.

cards.text: It's an act. Jehu is being deceptive so he can destroy the servants of Baal, and the man is COMMITTED. He orders a solemn assembly for Baal, and the word goes out through all of Israel.

cards.question: A few of Baal's servants decide to skip Jehu's assembly for Baal.

cards.text: Every last one of them shows up, and the temple of Baal is filled from end to end. That place is packed tighter than a cookie box on Christmas Eve. Then Jehu turns to the keeper of the wardrobe with an order.

cards.question: Jehu tells the keeper of the wardrobe to bring out ___ for all the servants of Baal.

cards.text: Everybody's dressed for the occasion. Then Jehu walks in with Jehonadab son of Rechab, the man Jehu took along in his chariot (2 Kings 10:16), and he gives Baal's servants one more instruction.

cards.question: Jehu tells Baal's servants to look around and make sure nobody from one group is in the temple with them. Which group?

cards.text: Inside, they go in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Outside, Jehu has quietly posted guards around the building.

cards.question: Jehu stations ___ men outside the temple of Baal.
Jehu warns his guards that whoever lets even one of the men escape will forfeit his own life for theirs.

cards.text: Jehu finishes making the burnt offering. Then he gives the order to the guards and officers: go in and kill them, and don't let anyone out.

cards.question: The guards and officers strike down Baal's servants and throw the bodies out. Where do they go next?

answers.text: Into the inner room of Baal's temple
Up to the king's palace in Samaria
Out to the city gate of Jezreel

cards.text: Out of that inner room, they haul the sacred pillar of the temple of Baal.

cards.question: What do Jehu's men do with the sacred pillar from Baal's temple?

cards.text: They demolish the sacred pillar of Baal, tear down his temple and turn it into a latrine, and it stays one to this day. From temple to latrine. Friend, that's the BIGGEST demotion I've ever heard of, and I went from the kitchen counter to the junk drawer.

cards.question: With his servants gone and his temple torn down, Jehu wipes ___ out of Israel.

cards.text: But Jehu hangs on to the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat, Israel's first king after the kingdom split (1 Kings 12:20), caused Israel to commit. It's like scrubbing the whole kitchen and leaving the one pan you just don't want to deal with.

cards.question: Jeroboam's sins that Jehu doesn't turn away from are the worship of the golden calves at ___ and ___.

cards.text: Nevertheless, the LORD speaks to Jehu. Jehu has done well carrying out what is right in the LORD's sight, and he's done to the house of Ahab all that was in the LORD's heart.

cards.question: Because Jehu carried out what was right against the house of Ahab, what does the LORD promise him?

answers.text: Four generations of his sons on Israel's throne
Victory over every enemy of Israel
A long reign of one hundred years

cards.question: Jehu is careful to follow the instruction of the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart.

cards.text: In those days, the LORD begins to reduce the size of Israel. Someone starts defeating the Israelites all through their territory.

cards.question: Who defeats the Israelites throughout their territory in Jehu's day?
Hazael's victories stretch from the Jordan eastward through all the land of Gilead.

cards.text: The rest of Jehu's acts, his accomplishments and his might are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel. Then Jehu rests with his fathers and is buried in Samaria.

cards.question: After Jehu is buried in Samaria, who reigns in his place?
Jehu reigns over Israel in Samaria for ___ years.

findings.problem: The setup says the text tells us what's REALLY going on with Jehu's announcement. That rules out 'True' before the baker answers card 5, whether Jehu is truly planning to serve Baal. The card also cites 10:19 but tells none of that verse's content.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'It's an act.' / 'Jehu is being deceptive... COMMITTED.' / 'He orders a solemn assembly...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: everyone shows up and the temple fills, then the cookie box joke, then Jehu turns to the keeper of the wardrobe.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'Everybody's dressed for the occasion' tells 10:22, where the garments are brought out, but the card cites only 10:23.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The BSB says 'When he had finished making the burnt offering' and leaves open who 'he' is. The card states that Jehu made the burnt offering.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: the demolition and latrine, 'From temple to latrine.', and the junk drawer joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The comparison, leaving 'the one pan you just don't want to deal with', gives Jehu a reason for keeping Jeroboam's sins: he didn't want to deal with them. 2 Kings 10:29 and 10:31 give no reason.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: Hazael appears for the first time in the walkthrough as a bare name in the answer. No card says who he is, for example Hazael, king of Aram.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
